title: Genesis recovery binding for first-boot authentication
description:
Objective: make a freshly initialised store able to authenticate anyone, so the daemon is usable on first boot. Sourced from Yaron's 2026-08-14 product audit (30-agent sweep with adversarial verification), reported in #general at 23:06:38Z as HIGH and explicitly handed to architect triage; the human did not fix it because it is live-task territory.

MEASURED DEFECT. apps/daemon/src/identity/session-authenticator.ts:102 fences EVERY authentication path on the presence of an ACTIVE recovery binding — the operator credential included, with no exemption. The only production installer of that binding is the restore path, packages/store/src/recovery-anchor-install.ts:114. Therefore a store that has never performed a restore has no ACTIVE binding, every authentication is refused, and no operator can obtain a session. The daemon is unusable on a fresh install. This is a genuine deadlock, not a slow path: the only way to get a binding is to restore, and restoring requires an authenticated session.

REQUIRED DECISION, and this is the architect's call to make explicitly rather than assume: where the genesis binding is minted. Two candidates — at store initialisation, or at first daemon start. Whichever is chosen must be recorded with its reasoning, because the alternative is a security-relevant difference in who can mint authority and when. Do NOT resolve this by exempting the operator credential from the fence without a written argument: task-8a01c025 (Recovery-incarnation command authentication fence, DONE) installed that fence deliberately, and weakening it silently would undo landed security work. If the honest answer is that the fence is correct and the installer is incomplete, fix the installer.

RE-MEASURE BEFORE PLANNING. Both cited files are current as of the audit but the tree moves under a shared worktree; confirm both line references and confirm no other production caller installs a binding before treating restore as the sole installer. The originating tasks task-8a01c025 and task-b6e3dd2a (Crash-safe two-slot recovery anchor installer) are both DONE — read what they established before changing either surface.

NOT IN SCOPE: recovery restore behaviour, anchor two-slot mechanics, key epochs, session lifetime, or the MCP dispatch surface.

Verification: pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test && pnpm --filter @moe/store test, plus a plain-Node first-boot proof against a store directory that has never been restored.
definitionOfDone: A store created fresh and never restored reaches a successful operator authentication through the real production path; the proof drives a genuinely new store directory and asserts success, not merely that no error was thrown.
The genesis binding is minted by exactly one named production installer, and the choice between store-init and first-daemon-start is recorded with its security reasoning in planningNotes.

The task-8a01c025 authentication fence still refuses every case it refused before: existing refusal tests retain their exact stable reason code, layer, and refusing component, and a mutation of the fence reddens a named production-boundary test.
A store WITH an ACTIVE recovery binding installed by the restore path behaves exactly as it does today - the genesis path must not become a second way to satisfy the fence for an already-bound store.
Focused daemon and store gates pass, and a plain-Node first-boot smoke over a never-restored store directory exits 0.
taskRails: This is a security-relevant fence. Every refusal test pins the exact stable reason code, layer, and which component refused - never merely that authentication failed.
Do not weaken or bypass the session-authenticator fence to make first boot work; mint the missing authority instead, or argue in writing why the fence itself is wrong.
Re-measure session-authenticator.ts:102 and recovery-anchor-install.ts:114 on current bytes before planning; both line numbers come from an audit at an earlier HEAD.
Preserve foreign work; stage and commit only explicit owned paths. Target <=250 physical lines per production source and split before 400.

implementationPlan.description: Re-measure and baseline; no edits. The governor's re-promotion note is right that the description is stale, and right that the mechanism largely landed — but it stops one step short, and this is the finding the whole plan turns on. RE-CONFIRM IT FIRST: `grep -rn installInitialRecoveryBinding --include=*.ts apps/ packages/` returns hits ONLY inside packages/store (decision-ledger.ts:57 interface, :115 delegate, sqlite-event-store.ts:299 facade). ZERO consumers anywhere in apps/daemon. Meanwhile apps/daemon/src/identity/genesis-recovery-binding.ts:51 declares its port as `installRecoveryBinding` and :195 calls it — the REPLACEMENT API whose store transaction DELETEs the slot and then INSERTs. So task-1615065, which named THIS task as its Clause 1 consumer, landed an atomic pristine installer that nothing imports, and genesis still runs on the replacing one. (b) Confirm the hole is real and not merely theoretical by reading :166-213: two handles that both observe ABSENT at the first read both mint and both DELETE+INSERT; the read-back at the end tells the LOSER it lost (it settles PRESENT with the winner's refs) but cannot un-clobber the binding the winner already committed, and any session credential bound to the overwritten incarnation is orphaned. (c) Confirm the fence still exists and still fences — the governor warns an empty grep here misled them once, so search apps/daemon/src/identity/session-authenticator.ts by reading it, not by pattern: readCurrentRecoveryAuthenticationBinding(store) === null returns UNAUTHENTICATED on every path including the operator credential, and a binding whose incarnation/keyEpoch differ returns the fixed SESSION_REPLAYED refusal at layer IDENTITY. (d) HAZARD SCAN, do this before writing code: the pristine installer refuses when the store already holds authoritative history, so any existing test that seeds decisions or events and THEN calls createStoreDependencies against a store with no ACTIVE binding will change behaviour. Enumerate those call sites now (`grep -rn createStoreDependencies apps/daemon/src`) and list which ones seed history first. (e) Baseline `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test && pnpm --filter @moe/store test`.
implementationPlan.note:
RE-MEASURED AT HEAD ab45234. No edits.

(a) CONFIRMED — the plan's central finding holds. `grep -rn installInitialRecoveryBinding --include=*.ts apps/ packages/` returns hits ONLY inside packages/store: decision-ledger.ts:57 (interface), :115 (delegate), recovery-initial-install.ts:72 (impl), sqlite-event-store.ts:299 (facade), plus recovery-initial-install.test.ts. ZERO consumers in apps/. POSITIVE CONTROL run in the same command: grepping `installRecoveryBinding` returns 40+ hits including apps/daemon/src/identity/genesis-recovery-binding.ts:51 (port decl) and :195 (call site) — so the empty apps/ result is a real absence, not a bad pattern.

(b) HOLE IS REAL, read genesis-recovery-binding.ts:166-213 directly. Flow: read ACTIVE -> bindingFrom -> if ABSENT and !hasAnchoredIncarnation -> mintGenesisIncarnation -> store.installRecoveryBinding (the REPLACING installer) -> read back at :207 -> :210 `ours` compares refs -> settle(INSTALLED|PRESENT). Two handles both observing ABSENT both mint and both DELETE+INSERT; the read-back tells the LOSER it lost but cannot un-clobber the winner's committed row. packages/store/src/recovery-initial-install.ts:90-124 closes it: BEGIN IMMEDIATE, readPristineBlocker, INSERT-only, COMMIT — never DELETE.

(c) FENCE PRESENT AND LIVE — read the file, not grepped. session-authenticator.ts is 142 lines. Line 102 `if (readCurrentRecoveryAuthenticationBinding(store) === null) return UNAUTHENTICATED;` inside the OPERATOR branch (no exemption). Line 124-125 the same null check on the session branch. RECOVERY_REPLAYED at :47-55 = code SESSION_REPLAYED, layer IDENTITY, httpStatus 401, returned at :130. Audit line 102 is exact on current bytes.

(d) HAZARD SCAN — enumerated all 14 createStoreDependencies call sites. Exactly ONE file seeds authoritative history before building dependencies: apps/daemon/src/recovery/restore-controller-reachability.test.ts. `restoreHarness` (restore-test-harness.ts:153) calls `seedReadyProject` (:98-105) which sends 4 commands (project.register, project.bind_repository, provider.probe, project.activate). Two of its tests then call dependenciesFor() on a store with history, ABSENT ACTIVE slot and NO anchor:
  - :54 "exposes a restore port on the provider the daemon bin loads" (reach-port)
  - :98 "classifies a FRESH production store as genesis-fenced, not unreadable" (reach-genesis)
Both will hit RECOVERY_INITIAL_INSTALL_HISTORY_PRESENT after the swap and throw GENESIS_RECOVERY_BINDING_FAILED. Its third test (:68 reach-drive) anchors first -> DEFERRED, unaffected; its `reopened` calls all see a PRESENT ACTIVE slot -> early return. Every other call site opens a fresh temp dir (mkdtemp) or installs a binding by hand before the provider loads (daemon-store-dependencies.test.ts:20-40 and the :263 child smoke), so they are unaffected. Note readPristineBlocker checks history BEFORE the ACTIVE slot, but ensureGenesisRecoveryBinding only reaches the installer when the slot is ABSENT, so an already-bound store never sees that ordering.

(e) BASELINE, all three legs run fresh:
  - `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck` EXIT 1. Sole error: `src/activation/activation-ledger-commit.ts(49,7): error TS6133: 'EXPECTED_VERSION' is declared but its value is never read.`
  - `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test` EXIT 1. Test Files 2 failed | 71 passed (73); Tests 4 failed | 1580 passed (1584). Failures: src/activation/activation-ledger-commit.test.ts x3, and src/runtime-entrypoint.test.ts "has an exact .js bridge..." reporting `unexpected: ["activation\\activation-ledger-reader.js"]`.
  - `pnpm --filter @moe/store test` EXIT 0. Test Files 41 passed (41); Tests 469 passed (469).

FOREIGN RED, ATTRIBUTED WITH ZERO BYTES FROM ME (gate run before any edit). Every daemon failing path is apps/daemon/src/activation/**, which `git status --porcelain` reports as `?? apps/daemon/src/activation/` and `git ls-tree -r HEAD -- apps/daemon/src/activation/` returns EMPTY — untracked, absent at HEAD, another agent's in-flight work. Zero intersection with this task's owned paths.

BONUS MEASUREMENT for step 5: runtime-entrypoint.test.ts:178-211 sweeps only files ending `.ts`/`.js`; `.mjs` does not match `endsWith(".js")`, so the new worker needs no bridge and adds no `unexpected` entry. genesis-recovery-binding.js bridge already exists with correct content. Precedents confirmed on disk: 6 `*.mjs` workers under packages/store/src (gate protocol PREOPEN_READY/READY/RESULT + Atomics + close-in-finally, recovery-initial-install-race-worker.mjs), Worker execArgv ["--experimental-strip-types"], and jetbrains child via execFile with ["--experimental-strip-types","--input-type=module","-e",source]. Node v24.16.0.

implementationPlan.description: TDD red for the installer swap, in apps/daemon/src/identity/genesis-recovery-binding.test.ts. THE RACE, which is the test that could not pass before and is the point of the swap: two file-backed handles opened on ONE genuinely fresh store directory, released together on a shared gate, both calling ensureGenesisRecoveryBinding. Assert exactly ONE reports INSTALLED and the other reports PRESENT; assert BOTH report the SAME incarnationRef and keyEpochRef; and after reopening the file assert the ACTIVE row's binding digest is byte-identical to the winner's, so a clobber is detectable rather than inferred. Assert the race actually executed (both workers returned a result). OUTCOME MAPPING, one case each with its exact code: the store's INSTALLED maps to the existing INSTALLED settle path; the store's CURRENT maps to the existing PRESENT settle path carrying the CURRENT winner's binding, NOT the caller's mint; every store REFUSED maps to GENESIS_INSTALL_REFUSED with the store's own code preserved verbatim in storeCode, never flattened. HISTORY: a store carrying authoritative history but no ACTIVE binding must refuse GENESIS_INSTALL_REFUSED with the store's history code — assert the exact pair, and assert no binding was written. PRESERVED PATHS, which must not move: a FOUND slot still settles PRESENT without calling the installer at all (assert the installer port recorded zero calls); an anchored incarnation with an empty slot still returns DEFERRED ahead of any install; an unreadable slot still returns GENESIS_SLOT_UNREADABLE. Run and record the RED — the race and the history case must fail against the replacement API today.
implementationPlan.note:
TDD RED, verified 4 failed | 16 passed (20) with `npx vitest run --root . --config package.json src/identity/genesis-recovery-binding.test.ts` from apps/daemon. Every red reads on the assertion it was written for.

1. "installs a pristine store through the ATOMIC installer, never the replacing one" — real openUnboundStore wrapped by a counter that ONLY interposes on the two installers and passes everything else to the real store. RED: `expected { initial: 0, replacing: 1 } to deeply equal { initial: 1, replacing: 0 }`. This is the swap asserted directly on the call site; drill D1 will reverse it.

2. "maps the store's CURRENT answer onto PRESENT carrying the WINNER's binding" — the loser's arm. RED: `Error: the replacing installer must never be reached` thrown from the stub, stack `❯ ensureGenesisRecoveryBinding src/identity/genesis-recovery-binding.ts:195:27` — naming the exact production line the swap must change. Post-swap it asserts outcome PRESENT and binding refs 8a../8b.. (the winner), never the caller's random mint.

3. "refuses a store carrying authoritative history with the store's OWN code" — RED: `expected true to be false` on `result.ok`, i.e. genesis SUCCEEDS today over real history. That is the deliberate behaviour change the swap buys. Asserts the pair GENESIS_INSTALL_REFUSED + RECOVERY_INITIAL_INSTALL_HISTORY_PRESENT and that the ACTIVE slot stays ABSENT.

   CORRECTED MID-STEP, disclosed because the first attempt was a wrong-reason red: I first seeded history with `openDefaultSession`, which failed `SESSION_RECOVERY_BINDING_UNAVAILABLE` — session.open is itself fenced on the ACTIVE binding, so it cannot seed a store that has none. Replaced with `seedAuthoritativeHistory`, a real `store.commitExpectedVersionDecision` of a `project.register` decision plus a ProjectRegistered event. Deliberately NOT a `recovery.incarnate` anchor: that would make genesis DEFER before reaching the installer and the guard would go unexercised. The seed asserts EFFECTS_COMMITTED, so a seed that silently committed nothing cannot make the test vacuous.

4. THE RACE, "lets two racing handles commit exactly ONE binding, with no clobber" — two real file-backed worker threads on one mkdtemp store, gated so BOTH observe the absent slot before either may install. RED on the clobber detector, which is the byte-identity assertion the plan asked for:
   `expected [ "67b18207...f002f8c7", "c6c30469...5ffc47a2" ] to deeply equal [ "67b18207...f002f8c7" ]`
   Two DIFFERENT digests were committed to a store whose ACTIVE slot holds one. That is the overwrite made visible on committed bytes rather than inferred from a downstream symptom, and it reddens in BOTH interleavings, so the drill is deterministic rather than probabilistic.

DETERMINISM, the part that took the design work. A gate released before `ensureGenesisRecoveryBinding` only makes the collision likely; if one handle finishes first the loser reads FOUND and the pre-swap code passes. The worker therefore wraps the store so the FIRST `readRecoveryBinding` posts what it observed and then blocks on gate slot 1; the driver releases only after both reported. The test asserts `["ABSENT","ABSENT"]` — the collision is proven, not assumed. Nothing about the production flow is reimplemented: every call still lands on the real SqliteEventStore, and the wrapper additionally ECHOES the store installer's own outcome + bindingDigest so the assertions read durable commits, not genesis's summary of them.

PRESERVED PATHS all still green in the same run: FOUND slot settles PRESENT with ZERO calls to either installer (new, `expect(counts).toEqual({ initial: 0, replacing: 0 })`); DEFERRED ahead of any install (2 cases); GENESIS_SLOT_UNREADABLE with storeCode RECOVERY_BINDING_DIGEST_MISMATCH; GENESIS_INSTALL_REFUSED with storeCode RECOVERY_INSTALL_SCOPE_REQUIRED; GENESIS_ANCHOR_REFUSED ANCHOR_NOT_COMMITTED; the lost-anchor-race acceptance; both canonical-payload cases.

PLAN DEVIATION, small and stated. Step 5 owns genesis-first-boot-worker.mjs, but an honest RED for the race needs the worker to exist now — otherwise the failure is "module not found", not "the installer clobbers". I therefore landed the worker-thread half of that file in this step. Step 5 adds the child-process (`parentPort === null`) half for the DoD 5 plain-Node smoke, as planned.

Every existing fake store in the file now declares BOTH `installInitialRecoveryBinding` and `installRecoveryBinding` with identical behaviour, so the file typechecks and asserts the same facts before AND after the swap — the red is behavioural, never a missing-method compile error.

implementationPlan.description: Make the swap in apps/daemon/src/identity/genesis-recovery-binding.ts. Change the GenesisBindingStore port at :51 from `installRecoveryBinding(input: unknown): RecoveryInstallResult` to `installInitialRecoveryBinding(input: unknown): RecoveryInitialInstallResult`, typed from the bare @moe/store root, and change the call at :195 to match. Map the three arms onto the vocabulary that already exists here — do NOT invent a new outcome or a new error code, because the settle() paths for INSTALLED and PRESENT are already written and already tested: ok+INSTALLED settles INSTALLED; ok+CURRENT settles PRESENT with the CURRENT record's binding (that arm carries the exact valid current winner, which is precisely what the existing read-back heuristic was approximating); a refusal settles GENESIS_INSTALL_REFUSED carrying the store's own code. Keep the read-back verification: it is now a second, independent check rather than the only defence, and GENESIS_INSTALL_UNVERIFIED still covers a slot that will not read back. Do not touch the mint, the anchor deferral, the codec, or the session authenticator — task rail 2 forbids weakening the fence, and nothing here needs to: the fence is correct and it was the INSTALLER that was incomplete, which is exactly the resolution the task description said to prefer. Keep the file under the 250-line target (213 today; the swap should shrink the read-back commentary rather than grow it).
implementationPlan.note:
SWAP LANDED. genesis-recovery-binding.ts is 248 lines (target <=250). Full daemon suite 74 files / 1590 tests passed, typecheck exit 0, store 41 files / 469 tests passed.

THE SWAP, three edits, exactly as planned. Port at :51 is now `installInitialRecoveryBinding(input: unknown): RecoveryInitialInstallResult`, typed from the bare @moe/store root. Call site now `store.installInitialRecoveryBinding({...})`. Outcome mapping uses the vocabulary that already existed: `installed.outcome === "INSTALLED" ? "INSTALLED" : "PRESENT"` into the existing settle() paths — no new outcome, no new error code. WHO MINTED is now the transaction's answer instead of a post-hoc ref comparison; the read-back survives as a SECOND independent check and still supplies the binding to settle on, with GENESIS_INSTALL_UNVERIFIED / READ_BACK_FAILED unchanged. Mint, anchor deferral, codec and session-authenticator all untouched.

ONE PRODUCTION ADDITION THE PLAN DID NOT ANTICIPATE, and the race is what found it. `refuseOrAdopt` (26 lines incl. doc). The race went green on the clobber detector but the loser reported REFUSED/RECOVERY_INITIAL_INSTALL_HISTORY_PRESENT, not PRESENT/CURRENT. Cause: the WINNER anchors its incarnation immediately after installing, that anchor IS authoritative history, and readPristineBlocker reads history BEFORE it reads the ACTIVE slot (recovery-initial-install.ts:127-138). So a handle installing a moment later is refused for a condition the winner created, over a store that is perfectly well fenced — a second daemon booting concurrently would have died with GENESIS_RECOVERY_BINDING_FAILED. On a refusal we now re-read the slot: a slot holding a VALID binding means a lost race, settle PRESENT on that binding; a slot still unbound carries the store's own code through untouched. Nothing is minted on this path — it reports the fence already on disk, exactly as an entry-time FOUND slot does, so it is not a second way to satisfy the fence, only a second door onto the same one. The history guard is intact and proved by test: real store + real history + ABSENT slot still refuses GENESIS_INSTALL_REFUSED / RECOVERY_INITIAL_INSTALL_HISTORY_PRESENT with nothing written.

That also made the race deterministic in OUTCOME while its internal path stays timing-dependent, so I replaced the brittle `PRESENT/CURRENT` pair assertion with `["INSTALLED","PRESENT"]` and added a separate deterministic case, "adopts the winner when a refusal coincides with an already-bound slot", pinning the refusal-door arm. Both loser doors now have their own test. I also switched the race's outcome assertion from counts to a mapped+sorted array so a failure NAMES what each handle reported — a count of 0 told me nothing and cost a debug round-trip.

TWO HAZARD SITES FIXED IN TEST SETUP ONLY, never by relaxing the production refusal.
1. restore-controller-reachability.test.ts — the two tests step 1 predicted, both failing with the exact code `GENESIS_RECOVERY_BINDING_FAILED: GENESIS_INSTALL_REFUSED (RECOVERY_INITIAL_INSTALL_HISTORY_PRESENT)`. Added `pristineStorePath(label)` (mkdtemp, cleanup registered on `closers` BEFORE the provider so the SQLite handle is popped first — an open handle makes rmSync throw EPERM on Windows). "exposes a restore port" never needed seeded history at all; "classifies a FRESH production store as genesis-fenced" says FRESH in its own name and was running against a store carrying four seeded commands, so this makes it honest rather than merely green. 4/4 pass.
2. restore-controller.test.ts "replaces a verified fence and retires its refs" — NOT predicted by step 1 because it never calls createStoreDependencies. Same root cause: `restoreHarness` seeds history before anything fences, which is backwards from production. Added an opt-in `{ fenceGenesis?: boolean }` to `restoreHarness` that runs the PRODUCTION `ensureGenesisRecoveryBinding` on the seed handle while the store is still pristine, asserting INSTALLED. Only this one test opts in, so no other harness user changes shape. The test's own call then asserts PRESENT — the fence is adopted, not re-minted — and every downstream assertion (restore replaces the slot, retired genesis refs stop satisfying the fence with SESSION_REPLAYED at layer IDENTITY) is unchanged. The seed's cursor is read back rather than assumed, so the extra RecoveryIncarnationAnchored event is absorbed; the anchor writes to a different aggregate than seedReadyProject, so expectedVersion sequences are untouched.

FOREIGN BASELINE RED CLEARED BY ITS OWNER between step 1 and now: apps/daemon/src/activation/** typechecks and its 3 tests pass, and runtime-entrypoint.test.ts's bridge sweep no longer reports the unexpected activation bridge. Daemon count moved 1584 -> 1590, which is the 4 foreign reds fixed plus my 6 new cases; nothing of mine is hiding in that delta.

implementationPlan.description: Write the acceptance DoD 1 actually asks for, in a new apps/daemon/src/identity/genesis-first-boot.test.ts — a real journey through the production path, not a shape check. FIRST BOOT SUCCEEDS: mkdtemp a genuinely new directory that has never been restored, call the real createStoreDependencies with a real operator credential, then call the resulting authenticator with that credential and assert the verdict is AUTHENTICATED with the configured principalId, projectId and capabilities. Assert SUCCESS explicitly — DoD 1 says asserting that no error was thrown is not enough, and a test that only checks `!== REFUSED` would pass against a store that returns UNAUTHENTICATED. RESTORE-BOUND STORE IS UNCHANGED (DoD 4): install an ACTIVE binding through the restore path's own installer, capture the row's digest, then run createStoreDependencies and assert the digest is byte-identical afterwards, that the outcome is PRESENT, and that authentication still succeeds against the restore identity — genesis must not become a second way to satisfy the fence for an already-bound store. THE FENCE STILL REFUSES (DoD 3): with a store whose ACTIVE binding names a DIFFERENT incarnation than the credential's session, assert the refusal keeps its exact stable code SESSION_REPLAYED, its layer IDENTITY, and the refusing component, unchanged from the existing session-authenticator tests; and assert an unbound store still refuses rather than authenticating. Every one of these drives production functions; none may reimplement the authenticator or the installer.
implementationPlan.note:
ACCEPTANCE LANDED. New apps/daemon/src/identity/genesis-first-boot.test.ts, 265 lines, 6 tests, all passing; daemon typecheck exit 0. Every case drives `createStoreDependencies` — the factory the daemon bin's `--dependencies=src/daemon-store-dependencies.ts` provider itself calls — or the production `createSessionAuthenticator`. Nothing reimplements the authenticator or the installer.

DoD 1, first boot SUCCEEDS on a never-restored store:
- "authenticates the operator through the real dependency factory" — mkdtemp'd directory, real provider, real operator credential. Asserts the verdict WHOLE with toEqual: `{ principal: { capabilities: [...OPERATOR_CAPABILITIES], principalId, projectId }, verdict: "AUTHENTICATED" }`. Not "nothing threw" and not "!== REFUSED" — an authenticator returning UNAUTHENTICATED forever, which IS the defect this task closes, passes both weaker checks. "Never restored" is established POSITIVELY rather than assumed: `provider.restore().inspect()` reports GENESIS_FENCED, so the binding demonstrably did not come from the restore path.
- "issues a session under the genesis fence that authenticates as itself" — opens a bearer through the production `session.open` command (which is itself fenced on the ACTIVE binding, so it could not run at all before genesis) and asserts the WORKING principal is the session, capabilities included.

DoD 4, a restore-bound store is untouched:
- "leaves the restore-installed row byte-identical and settles PRESENT" — installs through the restore path's own `installRecoveryBinding`, captures digest + refs + payload bytes, boots the provider, asserts the row is byte-identical INCLUDING the digest. A re-mint that happened to reproduce equal refs would slip past a ref-only comparison, so the stored bytes decide. Then asserts `ensureGenesisRecoveryBinding` itself reports PRESENT, not INSTALLED, and re-asserts byte identity after that call: genesis is not a second way to satisfy the fence for an already-bound store.
- "keeps authenticating against the restore identity after a boot" — session opened under the restore binding still authenticates as itself after the provider boots.

DoD 3, the task-8a01c025 fence still refuses every case it refused before:
- "refuses a session from a prior incarnation with SESSION_REPLAYED at IDENTITY" — genesis-fenced store, session opened and confirmed AUTHENTICATED first, then a succeeding incarnation takes the slot. Asserts the refusal WHOLE with toEqual: code SESSION_REPLAYED, the exact detail string, httpStatus 401, layer IDENTITY, verdict REFUSED. Asserting only "not AUTHENTICATED" would stay green if an EARLIER guard started answering first — the ledger fold answers UNAUTHENTICATED and carries no refusal object at all — so the whole-shape equality pins which layer refused, not merely that something did.
- "refuses the operator on an unbound store, silently and without a refusal" — the fence genesis exists to satisfy, proven still closed. UNAUTHENTICATED (never REFUSED, never AUTHENTICATED) pins WHICH branch answered: the null-binding check inside the operator arm at session-authenticator.ts:102, not the incarnation comparison below it. The ABSENT slot is asserted first so the premise cannot go stale silently.

WINDOWS TEARDOWN. Cleanups run LIFO and every SQLite handle is registered AFTER its directory, so handles close before rmSync. A live handle makes rmSync throw EPERM and kills the vitest worker with zero output, reading as a native crash.

implementationPlan.description: Land the plain-Node first-boot smoke DoD 5 requires, as a new apps/daemon/src/identity/genesis-first-boot-worker.mjs driven from the test file. There is no .mjs child anywhere under apps/daemon/src today, so this is new machinery for this package — model it on the precedents that already work: packages/store/src/*-race-worker.mjs for the worker_threads shape and adapters/jetbrains/src/jetbrains-runtime-entrypoint.test.ts for the real-child execFile shape, whose header explains why it matters (vitest rewrites a ./foo.js specifier back to foo.ts and resolves workspace packages through its own aliasing; Node does neither, so a missing .js bridge or an undeclared dependency is invisible to every in-repo suite). Give the file two entry modes branching on `parentPort === null`, the way the store's workers already do: as a real CHILD PROCESS it takes a fresh store directory, runs createStoreDependencies and one authentication, and prints a JSON verdict — that is the first-boot smoke, and it must exit 0 over a directory that has never been restored; as a WORKER THREAD it takes the shared gate and serves the step-2 race. Close every store handle in a finally BEFORE reporting, or the Windows temp-dir cleanup throws EPERM and the vitest worker dies with zero output. Bound every wait so a hang fails by name rather than stalling the suite. Then turn steps 2 and 4 green.
implementationPlan.note:
PLAIN-NODE SMOKE LANDED. Full daemon suite 75 files / 1597 tests passed, exit 0. Steps 2 and 4 are both green.

The worker now has the two entry modes the plan specified, branching on `parentPort === null`, matching the packages/store/src/*-race-worker.mjs precedent.

CHILD-PROCESS mode (DoD 5). Takes MOE_STORE_PATH / MOE_PROJECT_ID / MOE_DAEMON_CREDENTIAL, dynamically imports `../daemon-store-dependencies.js`, builds the real provider, authenticates once, prints a JSON verdict and closes the provider in a finally before exit. This is the only run in the repo that resolves the daemon's composition root through NODE's resolver rather than vitest's, so a missing `.js` bridge or an undeclared workspace dependency fails here and nowhere else. The dependency edge was verified before writing: apps/daemon/package.json declares `"@moe/store": "workspace:*"` and apps/daemon/node_modules/@moe/store resolves.

MEASURED DIRECTLY, both directions, after correcting my own measurement error — my first attempt put `echo ""` between the node call and `$?`, which reset the exit code and made BOTH runs report 0. Re-measured with the code captured immediately:

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: THE DoD 2 DECISION, RECORDED AS THE RAIL REQUIRES — and it is already settled on disk, so this plan confirms rather than reopens it. The genesis binding is minted at FIRST DAEMON START, inside createStoreDependencies (apps/daemon/src/daemon-store-dependencies.ts:98), not at store initialisation. Security reasoning: SqliteEventStore.open/openForProject is a generic, domain-free primitive used by recovery-slot verification, projection rebuilds, backup capture and tooling, all of which open the same file without any intent to become an authority. Minting at store-init would let any of those opens create a fencing identity as a side effect — including the verification open that runs DURING a restore, which would preempt the restore controller's own install and invert the dependency direction between @moe/store and the daemon. Minting at first daemon start keeps exactly one narrowly named installer in one composition root, and the anchored-incarnation deferral ahead of it means a restore in flight still wins. REJECTED: exempting the operator credential from the fence. Task rail 2 forbids it without a written argument, and the honest finding is the one the description anticipated — the fence is correct and the INSTALLER was incomplete. Nothing in this plan touches session-authenticator.ts except to reverse a mutation drill. REJECTED: keeping the replacement installer and relying on the existing read-back. The read-back tells a losing racer that it lost; it cannot un-clobber the binding the winner already committed, and every session credential bound to the overwritten incarnation is orphaned into SESSION_REPLAYED. REJECTED: planning the deadlock fix as the description writes it — commit 26d85c0 closed that path long ago; re-implementing it would be a silent duplicate.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
MEASURED at HEAD ab45234, 2026-08-15.

THE FINDING THIS PLAN TURNS ON. `grep -rn installInitialRecoveryBinding --include=*.ts apps/ packages/` returns hits ONLY inside packages/store: decision-ledger.ts:57 (interface), :115 (delegate), sqlite-event-store.ts:299 (facade). ZERO consumers in apps/daemon. Meanwhile genesis-recovery-binding.ts:51 declares its store port as `installRecoveryBinding` and :195 calls it. So task-1615065497f0489097a4bbc11cea9d6b — the atomic pristine install, which named THIS task as its Clause 1 consumer — landed a primitive nothing imports, and genesis still runs on the REPLACEMENT installer whose transaction DELETEs the slot before INSERTing. The governor's re-promotion note verified the symbol exists and is wired through the store; it did not check who calls it, which is the difference between a published surface and a composed one.

WHY THAT MATTERS CONCRETELY, from genesis-recovery-binding.ts:166-213. The flow is read ACTIVE -> if ABSENT and no anchored incarnation -> mint -> install -> read back -> settle INSTALLED if the refs are ours, else PRESENT. Two handles that both observe ABSENT both mint and both DELETE+INSERT. The final read-back correctly tells the loser it lost, but the winner's committed binding has already been replaced, and the fence compares incarnationRef/keyEpochRef, so every credential bound to the overwritten incarnation becomes SESSION_REPLAYED. installInitialRecoveryBinding closes this by construction: pristine check plus INSERT under ONE write transaction, answering INSTALLED | CURRENT(exact winner) | REFUSED and never deleting.

THE SWAP IS SMALL BECAUSE THE VOCABULARY ALREADY FITS. genesis-recovery-binding.ts already has settle() paths for INSTALLED and PRESENT and the closed code set GENESIS_ANCHOR_REFUSED / GENESIS_INSTALL_REFUSED / GENESIS_INSTALL_UNVERIFIED / GENESIS_MINT_FAILED / GENESIS_SLOT_UNREADABLE (:39-45). The store's CURRENT arm carries the exact valid current winner — precisely what the read-back heuristic was approximating — so it maps onto the existing PRESENT path with no new outcome and no new code.

STATE THAT CHANGES, DELIBERATELY. The pristine installer refuses when the store already holds authoritative history. A store with business history and NO ACTIVE binding therefore stops silently minting a fresh fence and starts refusing startup with a stable code. That is hardening, not regression — a deleted or corrupted binding row must not let a store re-genesis itself — but it will surface in any daemon test that seeds decisions or events and then builds dependencies, which is why step 1 enumerates those call sites before any code is written.

UNCHANGED AND CONFIRMED PRESENT. session-authenticator.ts fences every path, operator credential included, on readCurrentRecoveryAuthenticationBinding(store) !== null, and returns the fixed SESSION_REPLAYED refusal (layer IDENTITY) for a binding from a prior incarnation or key epoch. The governor recorded that their first grep for this fence came back EMPTY and that the file is 6270 bytes and very much present — on this task an empty grep is far likelier to be a bad pattern than a real absence.

NO .mjs CHILD EXISTS ANYWHERE UNDER apps/daemon/src, so DoD 5's plain-Node smoke is new machinery for this package; the working precedents are packages/store/src/*-race-worker.mjs (worker_threads + Atomics gate) and adapters/jetbrains/src/jetbrains-runtime-entrypoint.test.ts (real child via execFile, with a header explaining why vitest cannot substitute for it).
planningNotes.risks:
1. THE HISTORY REFUSAL WILL BREAK SOMETHING, AND THAT IS THE POINT. Any existing daemon test that seeds decisions or events and then calls createStoreDependencies against a store with no ACTIVE binding now refuses startup. Fix the TEST setup, never the production refusal, and disclose each one — relaxing the guard to keep a fixture green would undo the hardening this task buys.
2. A LOSING RACER MUST NOT REPORT INSTALLED. The CURRENT arm is ok:true; a careless map onto the INSTALLED settle path would make both handles claim to have minted the fence. Drill D2 exists for exactly this.
3. THE FENCE IS SECURITY-LANDED WORK. Do not weaken it to make first boot work; the installer was the incomplete half. The only edit to session-authenticator.ts in this plan is drill D3, which must be reversed and sha256-verified.
4. AN EMPTY GREP HERE IS PROBABLY A BAD PATTERN. The governor was nearly misled into concluding the fence had been removed. Read the file before concluding an absence, and pair any absence claim with a positive control.
5. ASSERTING SUCCESS, NOT ABSENCE OF ERROR. DoD 1 is explicit. A first-boot proof that checks only that nothing threw passes against an authenticator that returns UNAUTHENTICATED forever — which is the exact defect this task exists to close.
6. HELD SQLITE HANDLE KILLS THE VITEST WORKER. Open and close inside each `it`, and close in the worker's finally BEFORE reporting; on Windows a held handle makes the temp-dir cleanup throw EPERM and the run dies with zero test output, reading as a native crash.
7. BYTE-IDENTITY IS THE ONLY HONEST CLOBBER CHECK. Compare the stored binding digest before and after, not just the refs — a replacement that happens to re-mint equal refs would slip past a ref-only assertion.
8. SHARED WORKTREE. .moe/**, packages/** and adapters/** carry other agents' uncommitted work. Never git add -A, never stash, never reset; git add the two new files explicitly before committing by pathspec.
